header.title: Confidential recruiter pitch: Head of Platform role (via Brightline Talent)

evidence: On 1 October 2026 the user took a call from Dana Whitlock, a recruiter at Brightline Talent, about a Head of Platform role at a client she could not name yet.
The user told Dana they are interested, but that they have not managed more than one team before, and that they would want the equity terms in writing before going further.
The user agreed to a follow-up call on 8 October 2026, after Dana confirms whether the client will reveal its name.
pieces.body: On 1 October 2026, I spoke with Dana Whitlock of Brightline Talent about a Head of Platform opportunity at an unnamed Series C payments company headquartered in Lisbon with about 400 employees. The role would lead three platform teams of about 22 engineers across infrastructure, developer tooling and internal APIs, report to the CTO, and be fully remote within Portugal with optional Lisbon office access. Dana described a €145,000–€165,000 base salary, a 15% annual bonus target and unquantified equity; the client wanted a January 2027 start. Dana outlined a CTO call, system design session, leadership panel and reference check. I was interested but said I had not managed more than one team before and wanted the equity terms in writing before proceeding. Dana offered to email a one-page summary, and I agreed to a follow-up call on 8 October 2026 after she checked whether the client would reveal its name. Dana asked me to keep the client details confidential until the client agreed to disclose its name.
pieces.title: Brightline Talent Head of Platform opportunity, October 2026

header.title: Halvorsen Robotics hiring process (Senior Firmware Engineer)

evidence: The user is going through the hiring process for the Senior Firmware Engineer position at Halvorsen Robotics, a warehouse-automation company based in Trondheim.

The first step was a 30-minute screening call on 2 September 2026 with the recruiter, Tomas Berg. Tomas explained that the position is fully remote within European time zones, with one on-site week in Trondheim per quarter. He shared that the salary band is NOK 950,000–1,150,000 a year plus an annual bonus of up to 10%.

On 16 September 2026, the user had the final round, a video call with the VP of Engineering, Lene Haugland, who apologised for joining five minutes late. Lene described the firmware group as 14 engineers across three teams and said they expect to make a decision by the end of September. The user told Lene that their notice period with their current client is six weeks and that the earliest start date would be 2 November 2026.
pieces.body: In September 2026, I was in the hiring process for the Senior Firmware Engineer position at Halvorsen Robotics in Trondheim, after a referral from my former colleague Ingrid Sæther. Recruiter Tomas Berg screened me on 2 September; the position was fully remote within European time zones with one on-site week in Trondheim per quarter, and its salary band was NOK 950,000–1,150,000 annually plus a bonus of up to 10%. I had a technical interview with Ingrid and Aksel Moe on 9 September, then a final video interview with VP of Engineering Lene Haugland on 16 September. Halvorsen expected to decide by the end of September; I said my notice period with my then-current client was six weeks and my earliest start date was 2 November 2026.
pieces.title: Halvorsen Robotics Senior Firmware Engineer hiring process

evidence: The user felt weakest on the question about safety certification (IEC 61508), which they have no hands-on experience with, and noted it as something to read up on.
pieces.body: As of September 2026, I had no hands-on experience with IEC 61508 safety certification and wanted to read up on it after feeling weakest on that question in my Halvorsen Robotics technical interview.
pieces.title: IEC 61508 experience and learning goal

evidence: compared with their freelance work, the main draw is working on physical robots, and the main concern is the quarterly travel to Trondheim
The user has not yet decided whether they would accept an offer.

evidence: The user and their partner, Rui, spent two weeks in Japan from 11 to 25 April 2026: five nights in Tokyo, six in Kyoto and three in Osaka. It was their first trip to Asia.
In Kyoto they stayed at a small ryokan called Hanaori near Gion, which the user said was the highlight of the trip and where they would like to return.
Total spending was about €6,200 for both, slightly over their €5,500 budget.
pieces.body: Rui and I traveled to Japan from 11 to 25 April 2026, our first trip to Asia. We spent five nights in Tokyo, six in Kyoto and three in Osaka. We flew TAP from Lisbon to Tokyo via Frankfurt; the connection was tight and our luggage arrived a day late. Hanaori, a small ryokan near Gion in Kyoto, was my highlight, and I would like to return. I found Tokyo overwhelming because of the crowds. Vegetarian food was harder to find in Osaka than expected; shojin ryori temple restaurants in Kyoto were the easiest option. My favourite meal was at Tenkuu, a tempura counter in Osaka. I got a Suica card at the airport and topped it up twice. I would book the JR Pass earlier next time because its price rose the week before I bought it. We spent about €6,200 for both of us, slightly over our €5,500 budget.
pieces.title: Japan trip with Rui, April 2026

evidence: The user negotiated a freelance contract with Oakhurst Media, a podcast network based in Dublin, to rebuild the iOS client of its listener app. The contract was signed on 26 March 2026 and runs from 6 April to 30 September 2026.
The agreed day rate is €720, up from the €650 Oakhurst first offered; the user's own minimum for new clients is €700.

The scope is four days a week, with Fridays kept free for the user's other clients. Payment terms are 30 days from invoice, invoiced monthly; the user had asked for 15 days and accepted 30 in exchange for the higher rate.
pieces.body: I signed a freelance contract with Dublin-based podcast network Oakhurst Media on 26 March 2026 to rebuild the iOS client of its listener app from 6 April to 30 September 2026. The agreed rate is €720 per day, up from Oakhurst’s initial €650 offer. I work four days a week, keeping Fridays free for other clients, and invoice monthly on 30-day payment terms; I had requested 15 days but accepted 30 for the higher rate. My contact is head of product Siobhán Kelly, and the engineering lead is Marek Novak. The NDA bars me from publicly naming unreleased Oakhurst features, but I may name Oakhurst as a client in my portfolio. Intellectual property transfers to Oakhurst on payment, and either side may end the contract with 14 days’ notice. Siobhán asked for PDF invoices sent to the accounts address with the purchase order number, and I set up a template. An electronic signature was acceptable. I want to extend the engagement if the first release goes well.
pieces.title: Oakhurst Media freelance iOS contract, April–September 2026

evidence: The user is building Tern, a personal budgeting app for iPhone and Mac, as a side project with their friend Sofia Antunes, who handles the design. They started it in January 2026 and want a public TestFlight beta by the end of September 2026.

Tern imports bank exports as CSV and OFX files rather than connecting to banks directly, because the user does not want to store bank credentials or pay for an aggregator such as Plaid. The app is written in Swift with SwiftUI and SwiftData; the user tried Core Data first but switched in March because the migration code was getting too complex. Sync between devices uses CloudKit's private database.

Sofia wants a dark, high-contrast look; the user prefers following the system appearance, and they agreed to support both. The user spends Sunday mornings on Tern, about four hours a week. The biggest open problem is categorising transactions automatically: the user tried simple keyword rules and found them too brittle, and is now testing an on-device classifier. Tern will be free with a one-time €9.99 unlock for multiple accounts; there will be no subscription, because the user dislikes subscription pricing for small apps. The repository is private on GitHub under Sofia's account for now.
pieces.body: As of June 2026, I am building Tern, a personal budgeting app for iPhone and Mac, with my friend Sofia Antunes, who handles design. We started in January 2026 and aim for a public TestFlight beta by the end of September 2026. Tern imports CSV and OFX bank exports instead of connecting directly to banks because I do not want to store bank credentials or pay for an aggregator such as Plaid. It uses Swift, SwiftUI, SwiftData and CloudKit's private database for sync; I switched from Core Data to SwiftData in March 2026 because the migration code was getting too complex. Sofia and I agreed to support both a dark, high-contrast look and system appearance. I spend about four hours on Tern on Sunday mornings. After finding keyword rules too brittle for automatic transaction categorisation, I am testing an on-device classifier. Tern is planned to be free, with a one-time €9.99 unlock for multiple accounts and no subscription. Its GitHub repository is currently private under Sofia's account.
pieces.title: Tern budgeting app side project

evidence: the user dislikes subscription pricing for small apps
pieces.body: I dislike subscription pricing for small apps.

pieces.body: I gave “Offline-first sync without tears” at NordicSwift 2026 in Oslo on 24 September 2026. It was my first conference talk in English; previously I had spoken only at local meetups in Lisbon. The 30-minute talk plus Q&A covered conflict resolution with CRDTs in a SwiftData app, using Tern as the example, and drew about 250 people. I was nervous beforehand, and rehearsing five times with my partner helped a lot. The organisers covered my flight and two hotel nights; I paid for an extra night to see Oslo and had to ask the organisers for a USB-C to HDMI adapter. The slides are on Speaker Deck, and as of 28 September 2026 the recording was expected on YouTube in October. Feedback averaged 4.6 out of 5; several attendees praised the live demo, while two said the CRDT section was too fast.
pieces.title: NordicSwift 2026 talk in Oslo

evidence: La hermana del usuario, Lucía, se casa con Tomás Ferreyra el 12 de junio de 2027 en una estancia cerca de San Antonio de Areco, en la provincia de Buenos Aires.
Lucía le pidió al usuario que sea el padrino de la boda y que diga unas palabras durante la cena; el usuario aceptó, aunque le pone nervioso hablar en público.
La ceremonia será civil, a las 17:00, seguida de una cena para unas 120 personas.
pieces.body: Mi hermana Lucía se casa con Tomás Ferreyra el 12 de junio de 2027 en una estancia cerca de San Antonio de Areco, provincia de Buenos Aires. Acepté ser padrino y decir unas palabras durante la cena. La ceremonia civil será a las 17:00, seguida de una cena para unas 120 personas.
pieces.title: Boda de Lucía y Tomás Ferreyra en junio de 2027

evidence: El usuario piensa viajar desde Lisboa con su pareja, Rui, y quedarse tres semanas en Argentina para visitar también a sus padres, que viven en Rosario.
El usuario todavía no compró los pasajes; quiere comprarlos antes de fin de año para que salgan más baratos.
pieces.body: Para la boda de Lucía en junio de 2027, pienso viajar desde Lisboa con mi pareja, Rui, y quedarme tres semanas en Argentina para visitar también a mis padres en Rosario. Al 30 de julio de 2026 todavía no había comprado los pasajes y quería comprarlos antes de fin de 2026 para que salieran más baratos.
pieces.title: Viaje previsto a Argentina para la boda de Lucía

evidence: Lucía pidió que los invitados no lleven regalos y que, si quieren, aporten a un fondo para la luna de miel en Japón.
El usuario quiere que su regalo sea pagar una noche del viaje de luna de miel.
pieces.body: Para la boda de Lucía y Tomás Ferreyra en junio de 2027, quiero regalarles una noche de su luna de miel en Japón. Lucía pidió que los invitados no lleven regalos y que, si quieren, aporten a un fondo para ese viaje.
pieces.title: Regalo previsto para la boda de Lucía

evidence: El código de vestimenta es formal de verano.
La organizadora de la boda es Marina Ocampo, que pidió confirmar asistencia antes del 1 de marzo de 2027 en un formulario en línea.
pieces.body: Para la boda de Lucía y Tomás Ferreyra del 12 de junio de 2027, el código de vestimenta es formal de verano. La organizadora, Marina Ocampo, pidió confirmar asistencia antes del 1 de marzo de 2027 mediante un formulario en línea.

header.title: Interview loop at Verdant Grid (Staff Data Engineer)

evidence: The user completed the interview loop for the Staff Data Engineer role last week. The company builds forecasting software for electricity grids and has about 120 employees, most of them in Copenhagen. The loop had four interviews, on Tuesday and Thursday.

In the system design interview, the interviewer, Mette, asked the user to design a pipeline for smart-meter readings, and praised the user's enthusiasm and their questions about data quality. The hiring manager, Jonas, said the role is fully remote with a yearly team week in Copenhagen, and that the team works in Python and dbt on Snowflake. The user was weaker in the live SQL exercise and ran out of time on the last window-function question.

The salary range they gave was DKK 85,000–95,000 a month. The recruiter asked whether the user needed visa sponsorship (they don't, as an EU citizen) and whether they could share their resume as a PDF, which they did the same day. The user asked what "FTE" meant on the contract summary; it means full-time equivalent. They expect to hear back by Friday next week. The user likes that the product is about the energy transition, but is unsure about the pay, which is below their current freelance income. They would negotiate for 100,000 a month if an offer comes.
pieces.body: I completed four interviews for Verdant Grid’s Staff Data Engineer role on 6 and 8 October 2026. Verdant Grid builds electricity-grid forecasting software and has about 120 employees, mostly in Copenhagen. In system design, Mette asked me to design a smart-meter data pipeline and praised my enthusiasm and data-quality questions; I struggled with the live SQL exercise and ran out of time on the final window-function question. Jonas said the role is fully remote with a yearly team week in Copenhagen, using Python, dbt and Snowflake. The stated salary range was DKK 85,000–95,000 per month. I sent the recruiter my résumé as a PDF and expected to hear back by 23 October. I like the energy-transition product but am unsure about pay below my current freelance income; if offered the role, I would negotiate for DKK 100,000 per month.
pieces.title: Verdant Grid Staff Data Engineer interview loop

header.title: Recruiter call about a CTO role

evidence: Yesterday the user had a call with Marta Sousa, an independent recruiter, about a CTO position at Lumen Health, a 35-person Porto startup that makes appointment software for dental clinics. Marta asked the user to keep the conversation private, because the current CTO hasn't announced that he is leaving. The founders want someone who can still write code for the first year and grow the team from 6 to 15 engineers. The role pays €110,000 a year plus 1.5% equity vesting over four years, with a one-year cliff. It's hybrid, two days a week in the Porto office, which would mean commuting by train from Lisbon or moving. The company raised a €6M seed round in March and has about 20 months of runway. The stack is Kotlin on the backend and React on the web. There is no iOS app yet, and the founders would like the new CTO to start one.

Marta explained that the process would be a conversation with the two founders, a half-day with the team and a reference call. The user said the equity sounded low for a CTO and asked whether there was room to negotiate; Marta thought 2% might be possible. The user is interested in the iOS work and in being a CTO, but is worried about the commute and about the runway. Marta asked if the user had a portfolio site, and the user sent her the link. She mentioned that she mostly places fintech roles and that this one was an exception. The user wants to talk it over with their partner before deciding whether to continue, and told Marta they would reply by the end of next week. The call was meant to take 30 minutes and ran to an hour. Afterwards the user asked what a one-year cliff means, and it was explained that no equity vests until the first anniversary. They also noted that the founders had previously worked together at a hospital software company, which the user saw as a good sign for the product, and that the job ad they had seen earlier listed the role as fully remote, which Marta said was out of date.
pieces.body: On 1 September 2026, I spoke with independent recruiter Marta Sousa about a CTO position at Lumen Health, a 35-person Porto startup making appointment software for dental clinics. Marta asked me to keep the conversation private because the current CTO had not announced his departure. The founders wanted a CTO who would code during the first year, grow engineering from 6 to 15 people, and start an iOS app; the existing stack was Kotlin and React. The role was hybrid, requiring two days a week in Porto, despite an outdated fully remote job ad. It paid €110,000 annually plus 1.5% equity vesting over four years with a one-year cliff; I thought the equity was low, and Marta thought 2% might be negotiable. Lumen Health had raised a €6M seed round in March 2026 and had about 20 months of runway. The process would include founder and team conversations and a reference call. I was interested in the CTO and iOS work but concerned about the commute from Lisbon and the runway. I sent Marta my portfolio link and planned to discuss the opportunity with my partner before deciding whether to continue, then reply to Marta by the end of the following week. I saw the founders’ prior work together at a hospital software company as a good sign for the product.
pieces.title: September 2026 recruiter call about Lumen Health CTO position

evidence: The user plans to look up the founders on LinkedIn before replying.

Marta said the founders would like an answer before the end of September, because they want the new CTO to start in January 2027. The role comes with a €3,000 yearly training budget, which the user would spend on conferences.
The office is near São Bento station, about ten minutes' walk from the platform, so the train commute from Lisbon would be about three hours each way door to door.
pieces.body: In September 2026, I planned to look up Lumen Health’s founders on LinkedIn before replying about its CTO role. Marta said the founders wanted an answer before the end of September so the new CTO could start in January 2027. The role included a €3,000 yearly training budget, which I would spend on conferences. The Porto office was about a ten-minute walk from São Bento station, making the train commute from Lisbon about three hours each way, door to door.
